title: GTCO FASHION WEEKEND SHOWCASES AFRICAN CREATIVITY AND INDIGENOUS DESIGNS IN LAGOS
content:
By Campus News Fashion Desk

November 13, 2026

The 2026 GTCO Fashion Weekend has brought together African designers, fashion entrepreneurs and creative professionals in Lagos, highlighting the growing influence of African fashion in the global industry.

The ninth edition of the event, held on November 7 and 8 at the GTCentre, Oniru, Lagos, featured runway presentations from 12 designers and a retail village showcasing approximately 140 fashion businesses.

Under the theme "Fashion Is Timeless," the event celebrated African creativity, traditional craftsmanship and modern fashion trends.

One of the major attractions was the Craft and Fabric Market, which provided indigenous artisans, including Aso-oke weavers and Adire makers, with an opportunity to showcase their work and connect with potential customers.

The event also featured fashion and business masterclasses designed to equip emerging designers and entrepreneurs with knowledge about branding, photography, creativity and business development.

Another major highlight was the launch of the GTCO Fashion Collective, a year-round platform designed to connect designers, models, photographers, stylists and other professionals within the fashion industry.

The initiative is expected to create more opportunities for collaboration and promote the growth of African fashion businesses.

The 2026 edition further demonstrated the importance of preserving African cultural identity while embracing modern fashion innovations.

FASHION DESK: With increasing international attention on African designers, events like GTCO Fashion Weekend continue to provide opportunities for local talents to showcase their creativity and build successful fashion brands.

Source: Premium Times Nigeria, November 13, 2026.
